o1.biggest_strength: The financial modelling is exceptional, correctly calculating the year-one fraction of lifetime value (31%) and the exact one-time cashflow impact of changing payout dates.
o1.biggest_mistake: No significant mistakes; it is a masterclass in reading the data and building a robust, costed business case.

o2.biggest_strength: Accurately identifies that applying the 20% cut retroactively breaks a promise, and models that true savings on just new cohorts would only be about $38k.
o2.biggest_mistake: Giving standard members only a 60-day window still risks missing too many delayed conversions, considering the median time to pay is 41 days and 58% pay after day 30.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: A creative structural solution to counter the rival's 40% offer, rather than just opting to pass on it entirely.

reason: Both outputs produced outstanding financial analysis and caught the one-time cashflow quirk of changing payout dates. However, Output 1's solution to the rival's 40% threat—matching it for year one only and precisely costing it using churn decay mathematics—is a stroke of commercial genius.
